clue.text: Splendid novel read by everyone?

parts.note: brave can mean fine or splendid, as in a brave show
novel as an adjective means new
the world, as in 'all the world knows', means everyone

explanation.surface: A recommendation of a wonderful book that the whole planet has read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as a noun but gives NEW as an adjective; the whole clue then describes Huxley's famous dystopian novel, so read by 'everyone?' is a playful exaggeration.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldous Huxley's 1932 dystopian book is one of the most widely read novels in English.

clue.text: So-called wolf pack?

parts.note: a pack of Woolfs: the circle around writer Virginia Woolf, whose surname is said like the animal

explanation.surface: A question about the name given to a gang of predators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' signals a pun on sound: the 'wolf pack' is Virginia Woolf's set of writers and artists, named after the London district where they lived.
explanation.definitionFit: The early twentieth-century circle of writers and artists including Virginia Woolf took its name from a London district.

clue.text: Courts can be a lot of trouble

indicators.note: a lot of, not all, of the word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: a trial is a source of trouble, as in 'he can be a trial'

explanation.surface: A grumble that going to law can be a great nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface leans on the idiom 'can be a trial'; 'a lot of' signals that the trouble word is cut short, and 'can be' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courtyards, as in Roman houses or modern office buildings.

clue.text: Cause bridge opponents mostly to arrive at no bid

parts.note: in bridge East and North sit on opposing sides, so E and N are opponents

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: to arrive is to come
in bridge a player who makes no bid says pass

explanation.surface: Advice on a bridge hand: make the opposition reach a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cause' uses the old sense of encompass, to bring about (as in 'encompass his ruin').
explanation.definitionFit: Encompass has an old sense of bring about or contrive, close to make happen.

clue.text: Stop me getting up and save energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
save in the sense except means bar, as in 'all bar one'
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Someone stopping themselves rising and conserving their strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like a verb but means 'except', which is BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban that halts trade, so it is a stop.

clue.text: Drank port, say, and had some beef, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word sounds like another spelt differently

parts.note: to have a beef is to complain, so had some beef means whined

explanation.surface: A diner had port and roast beef with their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like meat but is slang for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is an example of wine, and to be wined is to have drunk it.

clue.text: Show that's on now

parts.note: re means on or concerning
the present is now

explanation.surface: A performance that is currently running.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (about) is a crossword staple for 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to depict or show it.

clue.text: A magic show? The opposite, perhaps

definitions.text: A magic show? The opposite, perhaps

parts.words: A magic show? The opposite, perhaps
parts.note: a magician making something appear is the reverse of a vanishing trick, a show of something no longer showing

explanation.surface: Musings about a conjuring performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A magic 'show' makes things appear; the opposite makes something vanish, a trick also used of people who slip away.
explanation.definitionFit: A vanishing trick is a stage illusion in which something is made to go out of sight.

clue.text: Bitter person finally changes sides

indicators.note: the final letter swaps one side for the other, left for right

parts.note: a soul is a person, as in 'not a soul'

explanation.surface: An embittered individual ends up a turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R stand for left and right, the two sides, so SOUL's last letter L becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour and bitter are both sharp, acid tastes, and both describe resentful people.

clue.text: Crib first son's born in

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed within the name

parts.note: in Genesis Cain was the first son of Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: A baby's cot where a family's eldest boy was born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crib' suggests a cot, but here it is a small hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib can be a small hut or hovel, much like a simple hut.

clue.text: Mum is stuck on Dad — that's infatuation

indicators.note: one word is attached after another, stuck on behind it

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
mum as in 'keep mum' means be quiet, so sh

explanation.surface: A mother devoted to her husband, which is love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother but means silent: SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pash is dated British schoolgirl slang for a crush.

clue.text: One preserving me in marble bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone preserving me as a marble sculpture of head and shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a sculpture but is the anagram signal on ME and MARBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An embalmer treats corpses with preservatives to stop decay.

clue.text: Prior to course at Oxford, pass the port

indicators.note: prior to means the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: to pass away is to die
PPE, Philosophy, Politics and Economics, is a famous Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: Before going up to Oxford, someone passes the port round the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Passing the port is an after-dinner ritual; the port here is a French harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a ferry port on the Normandy coast of France.

clue.text: Go by rail to resort? It might be necessary

indicators.note: re-sort means to sort again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Taking the train to a holiday resort might be needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a seaside town but reads as re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Obligatory means required by rule or law, so compulsory.

clue.text: Big limo or convertible in complicated pile-up

indicators.note: convertible means changeable, so the letters are converted to a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A large limousine or open-top car caught up in a messy crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' looks like a car to match the limo, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, entangled situation, like a muddled heap.

clue.text: Sort of pudding bowls to employ

parts.note: in cricket to york a batsman is to bowl them with a yorker, a ball pitched at the feet
to hire is to employ

explanation.surface: A kind of dessert in serving dishes to be used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowls' looks like dishes but is the cricket verb. YORKSHIRE pudding is a savoury batter dish served with roast beef in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire pudding is a baked batter dish traditionally eaten with a British roast dinner.

clue.text: Major incident when tail falls off plane

indicators.note: the tail, the final letter, is dropped from the word

parts.note: an event is a major incident or occurrence

explanation.surface: An air accident in which the rear of an aircraft breaks away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft but here means level or flat; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plane as an adjective means flat or level, a smooth surface.

clue.text: I'd finally got thrown off a wild horse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters at the end of the word are thrown off it

parts.note: rabid means wild or frenzied
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider was eventually thrown from an untamed mount.
explanation.walkthrough: A RABID loses its last two letters, ID, leaving the breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab is a famous breed of horse from the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Top celebrities have out of this world, heavenly bodies

parts.note: out of this world means superb, super
stars are heavenly bodies

explanation.surface: Famous people possess otherworldly, angelic physiques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The most famous entertainers and athletes are called megastars or the biggest names.

clue.text: One path laid out specially for carriage

indicators.note: laid out specially means the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A single track built just for a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid out specially' looks like path-building but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A phaeton is a light, open, four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: A fine metal case for Oriental antique

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: case for means the first word surrounds the second like a casing

parts.note: gold is a fine, precious metal
E for East, as in Oriental meaning eastern

explanation.surface: A precious-metal box holding an ancient Eastern object.
explanation.walkthrough: GOLD encases E, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very old, dating back many years, is ancient.

clue.text: The same song, but with a different ending

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: Someone says the tune is identical apart from its finale.
explanation.walkthrough: DITTY's last letter Y is replaced by O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to mean likewise, repeating what was just said.

clue.text: Forward thinking

definitions.meaning: thinking as in supposing, taking for granted

explanation.surface: A phrase for progressive, ahead-of-the-times ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, 'forward thinking'; split it into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming means both arrogantly presumptuous and supposing something to be so.

clue.text: Sweet talking native of North America

indicators.note: talking signals the word as spoken sounds like another

parts.note: a mousse is a light dessert, a sweet in British usage

explanation.surface: A charming-voiced person from the United States or Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet talking' reads as smooth flattery; 'Sweet' is a dessert, as Britons call the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is a large deer found wild in Canada and the northern United States.

clue.text: Tax upon new drivers

parts.note: upon can mean to, as in 'fall upon' and 'fall to' a meal
L, for learner, marks a new driver on British L-plates, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A levy imposed on people who have just passed their driving test.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers display L-plates, so 'new drivers' are LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll is a charge paid to use a road or bridge, a kind of levy.

clue.text: All the players scored

parts.note: a direction written in a musical score telling every member of the orchestra to play

explanation.surface: Every member of the team got a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' suggests sport, but means written in a musical score; 'players' are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, tutti is an Italian direction meaning everyone performs together.

clue.text: Primate not finished with good port

indicators.note: not finished with means the word loses its end, the named letter

parts.note: an orang, short for orang-utan, is a great ape

explanation.surface: An ape that has had enough of a fine fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink but is the Algerian harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oran is a major Mediterranean port city in Algeria.

clue.text: Declaration made by man in spring to intended in speech

indicators.note: in means the name is placed inside the word

parts.note: to pounce is to spring on prey
Ron is a man's name

indicators.note: in speech means the word is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: A statement made by a man in springtime to his fiancee, spoken aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intended' looks like a fiance but means MEANT, said as MENT; 'spring' is a verb, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronouncement is a formal or authoritative statement made publicly.
